planner_summary: The fresh prospective benchmark uses 30 new path and complete-graph fixtures of orders 3, 4 and 6, spanning five conductance scales. A calibrated baseline and two-load pilot select one common strength from {1/16, 1/4, 1, 4, 16}. The planner sees only scalar pilot intervals and the declared hardware envelope. The final acquisition is generated after selection and evaluated by the unchanged nonlinear interval inverse.
planner_interpretation: Both arms pay the same pilot cost and acquire a complete final plan: 11, 17 or 32 scalar readings at n = 3, 4 or 6, compared with 6, 10 or 21 for a bare canonical plan. Each budget uses 600 readings per arm. The two nonideal scenarios use 100 µA, 1 mS scaling, 1 ppm current and shunt errors, and up to 5 mΩ relay resistance. Eleven readout-limited pilots cannot resolve the required margins and fall back to t = 1. No false edge call or escaped true matrix occurs. The tested gain concerns this frozen finite-strength comparison, not arbitrary networks or equal elapsed bench time.
